standard: Acceptable visible refinement at application scale; not a numerical quality rating or production release approval.

front.note: The three vases now have smooth turned walls and softened rims, while rounded cupped petals replace the previous pointed star planes; this visibly improves the original coarse construction.

rear.note: The staggered heights and original stem positions remain recognizable from behind, with flower centers seated against their petal junctions instead of hovering above them.

detail.note: Full-size detail shows thin rounded petal edges with restrained cream highlights. The original brass centers remain shiny and stylized, but the petal finish is acceptable without changing its frozen material plan.

underside.note: Full-size underside confirms three closed ceramic base faces. The previous visible green lower stem ends and open outer bottom rings are gone.

clay.note: The clay view shows smooth continuous vessel silhouettes, rounded mouth construction and formed petals, while preserving the original compact arrangement and measured envelope.

front.note: The cylindrical jar bodies now read as smooth turned forms instead of visibly faceted tubes, with original wood lids and staggered heights retained.

rear.note: The reverse angle shows clean continuous body curvature and consistent lid seating without a new gap or protruding body section.

detail.note: Full-size detail shows the licensed wood grain on the original lids and smooth body highlights. Lid edge segmentation is minor at app scale; the inherited smoky material still reads opaque rather than clear glass.

underside.note: Three solid exterior bases replace the previously open-looking undersides, with continuous circular rims and no visible interior through the bottom.

clay.note: The clay view confirms smooth jar walls and connected lid silhouettes at the original footprint and height, providing a geometric improvement beyond the texture replacement.

front.note: The smooth closed ceramic vessel now holds visibly different thin utensil heads instead of four repeated blocks; the full-size front shows a turner, slotted head, rounded spoon and fork-like server.

rear.note: The alternate angle retains the original handle spacing and upright arrangement, with distinct head silhouettes and no detached piece above the crock.

detail.note: The detail view confirms a rounded vessel mouth and coherent grain on the handles. Its framing crops some head tips, so the full-size front view was also inspected to verify their shapes.

underside.note: The underside now has a continuous ceramic base with no view into the holder; the four original shafts remain inside its intended footprint.

clay.note: The clay view makes the thinner differentiated utensil heads and smooth cylindrical vessel clear, while retaining the original height and compact tabletop placement envelope.

front.note: The bowl now has a smooth spun shell and rounded continuous lip, removing the original coarse radial facets while retaining its three splayed supports and grate.

rear.note: The reverse angle keeps the original grate and wood arrangement seated inside the recessed bowl, with a more coherent curved wall and no new detached component.

detail.note: Full-size detail confirms smooth inner and outer shell transitions and a continuous rolled edge. The unchanged wood remains stylized cut stock; detailed bark, burning flames or a new log arrangement are not claimed.

underside.note: The underside now shows a closed smooth bowl base rather than the original open center, with all three existing support legs visibly meeting the shell.

clay.note: The clay view preserves the round recessed fire-bowl silhouette, thin rolled rim, grate and splayed leg construction, with visibly improved shell curvature at the original dimensions.
